title: SDK prompt bundling and rate-adaptive templates
author: Asha Kapoor
content:
Overview:

This playbook documents recommended SDK patterns, quickstarts, and rollout guidance for prompt bundling and rate-adaptive client templates. Prompt bundling is a technique that groups multiple short prompts or inference requests into a single API call to reduce per-request overhead, amortize KV cache usage, and improve unit cost. Rate-adaptive templates detect upstream throttling or increased latency and automatically reduce bundle sizes or switch to fallback paths.

Purpose:
- Reduce per-unit inference cost for workloads with many small, independent prompts (e.g., NLU classification, micro-generation, short completions).
- Maintain latency SLOs during bursty traffic by adapting bundle size and retry/backoff behavior.
- Provide SDK authoring patterns that are safe to roll out and observable.

When to use bundling:
- High QPS of short requests (< 300 tokens per item) where per-request latency is dominated by fixed overhead.
- Workloads tolerant to reordering within a response batch (or where responses can be correlated back to inputs).
- Not recommended where strict per-item latency guarantees (p99 < 100ms) are required.

Key tradeoffs and constraints:
- Bundling increases server-side token amplification and can temporarily increase tail latency for items at the end of a bundle.
- Causes larger individual RPCs which may interact with network MTU/timeout settings; ensure transport-level timeouts are adjusted.
- Must preserve model safety and metadata mapping for auditing and debugging (include input IDs).

SLO guidance (recommended defaults):
| Metric | Default target | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| 95th percentile bundle latency | 300ms | For bundles of up to 8 items, short prompts |
| Token cost per item | -15% unit cost | Measured vs 1:1 baseline with batching enabled |
| Error rate (server 5xx) | < 0.5% | Rollback if spikes > 1% during canary |

Quickstart: Python SDK example (bundling helper)
1) Install SDK: pip install redwood-sdk (example package name).
2) Configure bundle policy and telemetry options (see SDK config).
3) Use provided bundler helper to wrap per-item requests.

Code snippet (simplified):
```python
from redwood_sdk import RedwoodClient, Bundler, BundleOptions
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="${REDWOOD_API_KEY}")
opts = BundleOptions(max_items=8, max_tokens_per_item=512, max_total_tokens=2048, latency_target_ms=200)
bundler = Bundler(client, options=opts)

async def classify_items(items):
    # items: list[dict] each with {id, prompt, metadata}
    results = await bundler.map(items, lambda prompt: client.generate(prompt))
    # results is a list aligned with items by id
    return results
```

SDK configuration (YAML example):
| field | type | default | description |
|---|---|---:|---|
| bundle.enabled | boolean | true | Enable prompt bundling globally |
| bundle.max_items | integer | 8 | Maximum number of items per bundle |
| bundle.max_total_tokens | integer | 2048 | Max tokens across the combined bundle request |
| bundle.latency_target_ms | integer | 200 | Target end-to-end latency per bundle for autoscaling heuristics |
| bundle.adaptive | boolean | true | Enable rate-adaptive shrink/grow behavior |
| bundle.slow_threshold_ms | integer | 350 | If 95p > threshold, reduce bundle size by 1 |
| backoff.strategy | string | exponential | retry/backoff strategy on 429/5xx |
| backoff.base_ms | integer | 100 | initial backoff |

Example YAML snippet:
```yaml
bundle:
  enabled: true
  max_items: 8
  max_total_tokens: 2048
  latency_target_ms: 200
  adaptive: true
  slow_threshold_ms: 350
backoff:
  strategy: exponential
  base_ms: 100
  max_ms: 5000
```

API pattern and server expectations:
- The server accepts a combined request with an array of input records. Each record must include a stable input_id so results can be mapped back reliably.
- Example JSON payload structure: {"inputs": [{"input_id": "u1", "text": "..."}, ...], "bundle_meta": {...}}
- The server returns an ordered list of outputs aligned to the inputs array.

Rate-adaptive template behavior (runtime):
1) Baseline: start with configured max_items.
2) Observe 95th percentile bundle latency and 429/5xx rate in 60s sliding window.
3) If 95p latency > slow_threshold_ms OR 429 rate > 1%: reduce max_items by 1 (min 1), switch to conservative telemetry mode and tag traces with bundle_shrink=true.
4) If observed 95p latency < (latency_target_ms * 0.7) for 3 windows: increase max_items by 1 up to configured max_items.
5) Persist adaptive decisions into local SDK cache so restarts do not immediately revert.

Observability and telemetry (required fields):
- Trace/span tags: bundle.size, bundle.total_tokens, bundle.latency_ms, bundle.adaptive_action, upstream_status_codes
- Metrics to emit: bundler.requests_total, bundler.items_per_bundle.histogram, bundler.95p_latency_ms, bundler.429_rate, bundler.server_error_rate
- Logs: include input_id mapping on WARN/ERROR lines and a sampling policy for input payloads (PII redaction required).

Canonical fallback strategies (order of preference):
1) Reduce bundle size (fastest, stateless).
2) Switch to a cheaper model variant (if available and acceptable for quality).
3) Route to dedicated pool/region if capacity throttling detected for customer (requires routing config).
4) Switch to 1:1 mode for a short cooldown window if errors persist.

Rollout checklist (canary phases):
1) Unit tests: bundler unit tests + deterministic mapping tests for >95% coverage.
2) Local integration: run bundler against local dev runtime and stub server with 1k synthetic items.
3) Canary 1% of traffic (internal dev org) for 24h: monitor bundler.95p_latency_ms and bundler.429_rate.
4) Expand to 10% for 48h: run load tests to simulate double baseline QPS.
5) Full rollout: 7-day monitoring with automated rollback if server_error_rate > 1% OR 95p bundle latency increases by > 50% vs baseline.

Runbook: reaction to elevated errors after bundling rollout
1) Pager triggers if bundler.server_error_rate > 1% for 5m or 95p latency > 600ms for 5m.
2) On-call engineer (runtime team) steps:
   a) Query metrics: bundler.95p_latency_ms, upstream 429s, model queue length.
   b) Check deployment/host health and GPU utilization in dashboards (redwood-runtime-batches).
   c) If 429s dominate: flip SDK adaptive to aggressive shrink (bundle.max_items=1) via remote config and notify customers.
   d) If server errors dominate: rollback the bundling flag via feature-flag and schedule full postmortem.

Security and data handling notes:
- Always transmit a hashed input_id (SHA256) in telemetry to avoid sending raw user content. Maintain a server-side mapping only where legal/audit requires cleartext.
- Ensure PII redaction sampling is enabled in logs. Default: redact full prompt body for 99.9% of logs, allow 0.1% sampled traces for debugging with approval.

Appendix: example curl (combined request)
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate-bundle 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"inputs": [{"input_id":"u1","text":"Summarize: ..."},{"input_id":"u2","text":"Classify: ..."}], "bundle_meta": {"client_sdk":"py-1.2.0","bundle_id":"b-123"}}'
```
